paragraphs.source_en: Wrong. Trying harder is rarely the pathway to success. Trying smarter is the better way. It's the story of the shoemaker's children all over again. Too often, management people don't know how to manage their own careers. Their own promotional strategy is often based on the naive assumption that ability and hard work are all that counts. And so they dig in and work harder, waiting for the day that someone will tap them on the shoulder with the magic wand. But that day seldom comes. The truth is, the road to fame and fortune is rarely found within yourself. The only sure way to success is to find yourself a horse to ride. It may be difficult for the ego to accept, but success in life is based more on what others can do for you than on what you can do for yourself. Kennedy was wrong. Ask not what you can do for your company. Ask what your company can do for you.
